_meta.indication: QALSODY is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults who have a mutation in the SOD1 gene; approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in plasma NFL.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 233AS101 Part C (VALOR), noted as Study 101C
pivotal_trials.design: 28-week multicenter (32 sites, 9 countries), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized 2:1 to tofersen or placebo, stratified by fast/non-fast progressor
pivotal_trials.population: Adults (23 to 78 years) with weakness attributable to ALS and a confirmed SOD1 mutation (SOD1-ALS)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: change from baseline to Week 28 (Day 197) in the ALSFRS-R total score in the mITT population (joint rank test plus multiple imputation)
pivotal_trials.n: 108 randomized (72 tofersen, 36 placebo); mITT primary population n=60
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint negative: numerical difference of 1.2 favoring tofersen in ALSFRS-R change at Week 28 (-7.0 tofersen vs -8.1 placebo; joint rank + MI p=0.9689), not statistically significant. Plasma NfL reduced at Week 28 (67% difference in geometric mean ratios tofersen vs placebo, nominal p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were pain (42% vs 22% placebo), fatigue (17% vs 6%), arthralgia (14% vs 6%), CSF white blood cell increased (14% vs 0%), and myalgia (14% vs 6%). Serious adverse reactions included myelitis/radiculitis (6 patients), papilledema/elevated intracranial pressure (4 patients), and aseptic meningitis.
target_moa: Tofersen is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) that binds and degrades SOD1 mRNA to reduce synthesis of the SOD1 protein; gain-of-function SOD1 mutations are thought to cause toxic SOD1 protein aggregates in ALS.

advisory_committee.vote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee (March 22, 2023) voted unanimously 9 to 0 that the available evidence supports that reduction in NfL is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Reduction in plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) concentration, accepted as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in SOD1-ALS.

citations.quote: The Division has determined that the observed reduction in plasma NfL concentration is acceptable as a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in patients with SOD1-ALS.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Complete Study 233AS303 (ATLAS), a Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trial in presymptomatic adults with a confirmed SOD1 mutation, to verify clinical benefit (PMR 4436-1).

citations.quote: 4436-1 In order to verify the clinical benefit of tofersen, complete Study 233AS303 (ATLAS), "A Phase 3 Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial With a Longitudinal Natural History Run-In and Open-Label Extension to Evaluate BIIB067 Initiated in Clinically Presymptomatic Adults With a Confirmed Superoxide Dismutase 1 Mutation".

basis.text: The NDA was granted Priority review.

citations.quote: The NDA was granted Priority review and was reviewed under The Program due to its status as a new molecular entity.

summary.text: Tofersen received Fast Track (2015) and Orphan Drug designation; a Breakthrough Therapy request was denied. The NDA received Priority review and was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 based on reduction in plasma NfL as a surrogate reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with a required confirmatory Phase 3 trial (ATLAS).

citations.quote: The IND was allowed to proceed and Fast Track designation was granted on December 23, 2015.
The NDA was granted Priority review and was reviewed under The Program due to its status as a new molecular entity.
It is approved under accelerated approval pursuant to section 506(c) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) and 21 CFR 314.510, effective on the date of this letter

requirement.text: 4436-1: Complete Study 233AS303 (ATLAS), a Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trial in clinically presymptomatic adults with a confirmed SOD1 mutation, to verify clinical benefit; primary endpoint is proportion with emergence of clinically manifested ALS.
